body:
I had to think about this flag a bit.

Its easy enough to see on the ElectronicStructureProblem, where there is a method to return a list or dictionary that we return a list as per the user expects since there are users calling that directly, using the top half of the stack so to speak, to get operators from a molecule which they then pass onto VQE.

If the user passes in a List of aux ops here shouldn't we just handle it as a list all the way down and back up the stack. This would be compatible with what is there now. If they pass in a dict, would be new code, then results would be in dict form too. I guess the flag comes into play if the user does not themselves supply any additional aux ops in that we can state things will become a dict in the future and this flag allows you to transition your code in that direction already by setting this true.

It does seem like a bit of extra complexity. I wonder if some single global flag would be better than adding/removing from a bunch of the APIs, where we look to that one single flag on how to behave in the absence of any other clues.

Right now, this `ListOrDict` class is simply a wrapper which simplifies the iteration over whatever original type the operator were in. I did this because otherwise a lot of code would be duplicated in the internals of the `QubitConverter`.
In the end of the converter, the objects get's unwrapped anyways, before continuing with the rest of the stack.

That said, I agree that if we had a utility class such as this one on the Terra level, we would not need to do the unwrapping and could simply use that type everywhere. However, introducing such a class on the Terra level + using it as the type of how to pass operators back and forth would require exposing this utility class as part of the public API. I am not sure whether that is something we (or the Terra devs) want..
